summary: Duplicate sustainability surcharge applied after billing-rule deployment during org migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that their March monthly invoice includes a sustainability surcharge line applied twice for the same hourly reserved capacity blocks. The duplicate surcharge only appears after an org-consolidation migration was executed last week. Customer believes this is an overcharge and requests a credit and an audit explanation.

Impact:
- Finalized invoice shows two identical sustainability surcharge line items for multiple days (small per-hour amounts but aggregated to ~USD 3,250).
- Customer is enterprise tier and flagged billing as high priority for accounting reconciliation.

Environment:
prod | us-east

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Org consolidation ran on 2026-03-07 (internal migration ID: org-merge-2026-03-07).
2) Customer continued normal reserved capacity usage in us-east.
3) Preliminary invoice (generated 2026-03-10) includes duplicate surcharge lines for 2026-03-08 through 2026-03-11.

Attachments: billing CSV extract and invoice PDF provided by customer (attached in ticket).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 — Maya Thompson (Support): Acknowledged receipt. Escalating to Billing and SRE for investigation. Asking customer for CSV extract and invoice PDF.

2026-03-10 11:02 — Samir Patel (Customer): Provided CSV extract and invoice PDF. Notes: duplicate lines have identical rate_id and time windows; happened only after the org-merge job. Please advise ASAP, we close books on 2026-03-15.

2026-03-11 08:44 — Ethan Rivera (Billing): Running reconciliation queries against ledger and postback stream. Initial hypothesis: two effective rate-tag assignments during migration caused both legacy and migrated tags to be applied in hourly apportionment step.

2026-03-12 16:30 — Priya Verma (SRE): Confirmed duplicate postbacks for sustainability_surcharge tag between 2026-03-07T02:00Z and 2026-03-08T06:00Z in postback-reconciler logs. Seen on worker-node-7 and worker-node-3. Suspect idempotency key collision during the migration replay.

2026-03-13 10:20 — Maya Thompson (Support): Notified customer that we will provision a provisional credit for the duplicated lines while we complete the audit. Pending permanent reconciliation after root cause fix.
investigation_notes: Query run: SELECT count(*) FROM postback_events WHERE tag='sustainability_surcharge' AND org_id='greenbox' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-07' AND '2026-03-09' -> returned 384 (expected ~192).

Log snippet from postback-reconciler (worker-node-7): 'Received postback id=pb-9a2f migration_replay=true idempotency=null applying tag sustainability_surcharge', then same id processed again after 2s with different internal_tag_alias.

Observed that migration job org-merge-2026-03-07 set a temporary alias mapping for rate tags (alias_sustain_20260307) and a background postback replayer retried earlier unacknowledged postbacks without idempotency keys, resulting in double-apply when translated to canonical tag.

Billing engine: hourly_apportionment step applies surcharges by joining postback_events -> rate_tags -> invoice_lines. Duplicate postbacks created duplicate joins producing two invoice line entries with same meta (rate_id r-sustain-01).
Repro on staging: Replayed a small window with migration aliasing enabled; reproduced duplicate surcharge lines in provisional invoice preview.
resolution:
Workaround and next steps: 1) Issued provisional credit of USD 3,250 on 2026-03-13 applied to the account (visible in billing ledger). 2) Hotfix merged to billing service to enforce idempotency keys on migration replay (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/482). 3) Scheduled a run of the postback replayer with idempotency safeguards to dedupe and reconcile ledger entries on 2026-03-14; permanent reconciliation will update finalized invoice if necessary. 4) Customer invited to a post-mortem/ledger audit session on 2026-03-16.

Follow-up items: refund if reconciliation shows credit insufficient, tighten migration runbook to include idempotency checks (Confluence runbook updated), and add automated regression test to prevent duplicate surcharge application.
